recipes.name: Sunflower Butter Banana Roll-Ups
recipes.summary: A tortilla spread with sunflower seed butter, rolled around a whole banana and sliced into pinwheels. Peanut-free and tree-nut-free, so it suits nut-free schools.

ingredients.prep: or peanut butter where nuts are allowed

steps: Spread 2 tablespoons of sunflower seed butter over each tortilla, almost to the edge. Drizzle with a teaspoon of honey and a pinch of cinnamon if you like.
Peel the bananas and cut each one in half crosswise. Lay a banana half near one edge of each tortilla.
Roll the tortilla up tightly around the banana. The spread holds it closed.
Slice each roll into 4 pinwheels with a sharp knife, or leave it whole and cut it in half. Pack the pieces snugly in a container so they don’t unroll.
recipes.make_ahead: Best made the morning of; the banana darkens after a day. Spread the tortillas the night before and add the banana in the morning.

freezer.text: Bananas turn soft and brown when frozen this way.

leftovers.text: Whatever comes home uneaten from a lunch box gets thrown away, along with used bags and wrappers (USDA).

recipes.kids: Kids as young as 4 can spread and roll these themselves. Older kids can slice them with a grown-up watching.

swaps.nut_free: Sunflower seed butter is free of peanuts and tree nuts. Check the label for “made in a facility” warnings if your school asks.
swaps.apple: Use thin apple slices instead of banana.

prep_day.ahead: Spread the tortillas the night before.

recipes.name: Ranch Chicken Lunch Wraps
recipes.summary: Shredded chicken tossed with ranch, rolled up with crisp lettuce and cheddar. A good use for leftover roast or rotisserie chicken.

ingredients.prep: meat only, shredded (or leftover roast chicken)

steps: Use chicken that has been kept in the refrigerator and is no more than 3 to 4 days old (USDA). Toss the shredded chicken with the ranch.
Lay a lettuce leaf down the middle of each tortilla. Top with a quarter of the chicken, the cheddar and the tomatoes.
Fold in the sides, then roll up tightly from the bottom. Wrap each one in plastic wrap or foil, seam side down, and cut it in half on a slant.

Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Make the chicken mixture up to 2 days ahead and keep it in the refrigerator. Roll the wraps the night before or that morning.

freezer.text: Lettuce and ranch don’t freeze well.

leftovers.text: Whatever comes home uneaten from a lunch box gets thrown away, along with used bags and wrappers (USDA).

recipes.kids: Kids can shred the chicken with two forks and roll their own wraps.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free dressing and skip the cheese.
swaps.veggie: Use a drained can of chickpeas, lightly mashed, instead of chicken.

prep_day.ahead: Shred the chicken and toss it with ranch.

recipes.name: Pizza Pinwheels
recipes.summary: Pizza dough rolled up with sauce, mozzarella and pepperoni, sliced and baked. Good cold, which makes them a lunch box favorite.

ingredients.prep: about 1 lb, thawed in the refrigerator (or homemade)

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment.
On a lightly floured counter, roll the dough into a rectangle about 10 by 14 inches. If it springs back, let it rest 5 minutes and try again.
Spread the sauce over the dough, leaving a 1-inch strip bare along one long edge. Sprinkle with the cheese and seasoning, and lay the pepperoni on top.
Starting from the long edge with sauce, roll the dough up tightly. Pinch the bare edge to seal it.
Cut the roll into 12 slices with a sharp knife and set them cut side up on the baking sheet. Brush the tops with oil.
Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until golden and the cheese bubbles. Cool on the pan.

Refrigerate within 2 hours. Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Bake on the weekend; they keep 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator.

freezer.text: Freeze baked pinwheels in a bag up to 2 months. Move what you need to the refrigerator the night before.

leftovers.text: Refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 to 4 days.

recipes.kids: Kids can spread the sauce, sprinkle the cheese and lay out the pepperoni. A grown-up slices the roll.

swaps.veggie: Use diced bell peppers and spinach instead of pepperoni.
swaps.from_scratch: Use half a batch of the from-scratch pizza dough.

recipes.name: Cracker Stacker Lunch Box
recipes.summary: A homemade version of the store-bought cracker kits: crackers, cheese and turkey to stack, with cucumber and grapes on the side.

ingredients.prep: cut into squares the size of the crackers

steps: Slice the cheese into thin squares about the size of the crackers. Cut each turkey slice into 4 squares.
Slice the cucumber into rounds. For toddlers and preschoolers, cut grapes and cherry tomatoes into small pieces; whole, they are a choking hazard for young children (CDC).
In each divided container, put 6 crackers in one section (to keep them crisp, away from the wet foods), the cheese and turkey in another, and the cucumber and grapes in the rest.

Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the cheese, turkey and cucumber up to 2 days ahead and keep them in the refrigerator in separate containers. Pack the crackers in the morning.

leftovers.text: Whatever comes home uneaten from a lunch box gets thrown away, along with used bags and wrappers (USDA).

recipes.kids: This is a good first lunch for kids to pack themselves: count out the crackers and fill each section.

swaps.veggie: Use hummus and extra cheese instead of turkey.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and add a dip such as hummus or white bean dip.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the cheese, turkey and vegetables.

recipes.name: Nut-Free Sunflower Oat Energy Bites
recipes.summary: No-bake oat bites held together with sunflower seed butter and honey, with mini chocolate chips. Made for nut-free classrooms.
steps: Stir the sunflower butter, honey and vanilla together in a bowl until smooth.
Add the oats, ground flaxseed, chocolate chips and salt. Stir until everything is coated. If it’s too sticky to roll, add a spoonful more oats.
Chill the bowl 20 to 30 minutes so the mixture firms up.
Roll into 24 balls about 1 inch across, with damp hands. Keep them in a covered container in the refrigerator.

freezer.text: Freeze up to 3 months; they thaw in the lunch box by lunchtime.

recipes.kids: Kids can measure, stir and roll these. No stove or oven needed.

swaps.nut_free: Sunflower seed butter keeps these free of peanuts and tree nuts. Check the chocolate chip label too.
swaps.dairy_free: Use dairy-free chocolate chips, or raisins.
swaps.honey: Use maple syrup; for children under 1 year, don’t use honey.

prep_day.ahead: Make a batch for the week.

recipes.name: Mini Corn Dog Muffins
recipes.summary: Sweet cornbread batter baked around rounds of hot dog in a mini muffin pan. All the fun of a corn dog, no frying.

ingredients.prep: plus a little for the pan

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Grease the mini muffin cups well.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl. In another bowl, whisk the milk, egg and oil. Stir the wet into the dry just until no flour shows.
Spoon a tablespoon of batter into each cup and press a round of hot dog into the center of each.
Bake 13 to 15 minutes, until golden and a toothpick in the cornbread comes out clean. The hot dog in the center should reach 165°F (USDA).

Cool 5 minutes, then loosen with a butter knife. Refrigerate within 2 hours. Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Bake on the weekend; they keep 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator.

freezer.text: Freeze up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator.

leftovers.text: Refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days.

recipes.kids: Kids can stir the batter and press a hot dog round into each cup. For young children, cut the muffins in quarters: hot dog pieces are a choking hazard (CDC).

swaps.veggie: Use plant-based hot dogs, or corn kernels and cheddar instead.

recipes.name: Black Bean and Corn Quesadilla Triangles
recipes.summary: Crisp tortillas folded around cheese, black beans and corn. Good warm for dinner and good cold in a lunch box the next day.
steps: Mash about half the beans with a fork, then stir in the rest of the beans, the corn and cumin.
Spread a quarter of the beans over 4 tortillas. Sprinkle with cheese and top with the other tortillas.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and brush it with a little oil. Cook one quesadilla at a time, 2 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese melts.

Cut each into 4 triangles. For lunches, cool them on a rack, refrigerate within 2 hours, and pack with a little salsa. Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Make them the night before and refrigerate.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked, cooled triangles up to 2 months, with parchment between them.

leftovers.text: Refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days.

recipes.kids: Kids can mash the beans and build the quesadillas. A grown-up handles the hot skillet.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free cheese, or mash in avocado instead.

recipes.name: Hard-Cooked Eggs for the Week
recipes.summary: Six eggs cooked until the whites and yolks are firm, cooled fast and kept in the refrigerator for the week’s lunches.
steps: Set the eggs in a single layer in a saucepan and add cold water to cover them by 1 inch.
Bring to a full boil over high heat. Cover the pan, take it off the heat, and let the eggs stand 12 minutes for large eggs (15 for extra-large).
Lift the eggs into a bowl of ice water and leave them 5 minutes, until cool enough to hold.
Refrigerate them within 2 hours. Use hard-cooked eggs within 1 week, in or out of the shell (USDA). Peel them under running water when you need them.

Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Cook a batch on Sunday for the week.

freezer.text: Cooked egg whites turn rubbery in the freezer.

recipes.kids: Kids can peel cooled eggs. Tap the egg all over, then peel it under running water.

swaps.deviled: Halve and fill them with the yolks mashed with mayonnaise and mustard; keep these cold too.

recipes.name: Strawberry Yogurt Bark
recipes.summary: Greek yogurt sweetened with a little honey, spread on a pan with strawberries, frozen and broken into pieces.
steps: Line a baking sheet with parchment. Stir the yogurt, honey and vanilla together.
Spread the yogurt on the parchment about ¼ inch thick. Scatter the strawberries and chocolate chips over it and press them in lightly.
Freeze at least 3 hours, until firm, then break it into about 16 pieces. Keep them in a freezer bag.
Pack a few pieces in a small container, frozen, next to the other cold foods. They soften by lunchtime; this is a cold food, not an ice pack, so still use two cold sources (USDA).

freezer.text: Keep it frozen up to 1 month.

recipes.kids: Kids can spread the yogurt and decorate it with fruit.

swaps.berries: Use blueberries, raspberries or diced mango.

prep_day.ahead: Freeze a pan on the weekend.

recipes.name: Applesauce Oat Muffins
recipes.summary: Soft, lightly sweet muffins made with applesauce, oats and cinnamon. Nut-free, and sturdy enough to ride in a backpack.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line a 12-cup muffin pan.
Whisk the flour, oats, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the applesauce, egg, oil and milk. Stir them into the dry ingredients just until combined, then fold in the raisins.
Divide among the cups and bake 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool on a rack.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 2 days on the counter in a covered container, or 5 days in the refrigerator.

freezer.text: Freeze up to 3 months. A frozen muffin thaws in the lunch box by lunchtime.

recipes.kids: Kids can measure, stir and fill the liners. A grown-up handles the hot pan.

swaps.egg_free: Use 1 tablespoon ground flaxseed stirred into 3 tablespoons water, left 5 minutes.

recipes.name: Cucumber Cream Cheese Sandwiches
recipes.summary: Whole wheat bread with herby cream cheese and thin cucumber slices, cut into strips or triangles. Cool and crunchy.
steps: Stir the cream cheese with the dill.
Slice the cucumber thin and lay the slices on paper towels for a few minutes to soak up extra water, so the bread doesn’t get soggy.
Spread the cream cheese on all 8 slices of bread, edge to edge (it keeps the cucumber from wetting the bread). Layer cucumber on 4 slices, sprinkle with a little salt, and close the sandwiches.

Cut into triangles or strips. Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the dill cream cheese up to 5 days ahead. Assemble the sandwiches the morning you pack them.

leftovers.text: Whatever comes home uneaten from a lunch box gets thrown away, along with used bags and wrappers (USDA).

recipes.kids: Kids can spread the cream cheese and layer the cucumbers.

swaps.dairy_free: Use hummus instead of cream cheese.

recipes.name: Mini Chicken Meatball Bites
recipes.summary: Small, tender chicken meatballs with Parmesan and herbs. Pack them cold with a dip, or hot in a preheated insulated container.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Brush it with the oil.
Mix the chicken, breadcrumbs, egg, Parmesan, garlic powder, Italian seasoning and salt with your hands or a fork, just until combined. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Roll into about 30 balls, 1 inch across (wet hands help), and set them on the pan.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes, until lightly browned and a food thermometer reads 165°F in the center of a meatball (USDA).

Cool, then refrigerate within 2 hours. For a cold lunch, pack them with the marinara as a dip. Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).
For a hot lunch, reheat them in sauce to 165°F, fill an insulated food jar that you have warmed with boiling water for a few minutes, and keep it closed until lunch (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Bake on the weekend; they keep 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked meatballs on a tray, then bag them, up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days. Reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can roll the meatballs with clean hands and wash them well after.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free breadcrumbs or quick oats.

recipes.name: Turkey, Apple and Cheddar Sandwiches
recipes.summary: Sliced turkey and sharp cheddar with thin, crisp apple slices on whole wheat. Sweet, salty and crunchy.
steps: Toss the apple slices with the lemon juice so they don’t turn brown.
Spread mayonnaise or mustard on 4 slices of bread. Layer 3 slices of turkey, a slice of cheddar and a few apple slices on each, and close with the other bread.

Cut in half and wrap. Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble the night before and keep in the refrigerator; the lemon keeps the apple fresh.

freezer.text: Apple and mayonnaise don’t freeze well.

leftovers.text: Whatever comes home uneaten from a lunch box gets thrown away, along with used bags and wrappers (USDA).

recipes.kids: Kids can layer the sandwiches. A grown-up slices the apple.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and add lettuce.

recipes.name: Hot Thermos Ravioli
recipes.summary: Cheese ravioli in tomato sauce, packed piping hot in a preheated insulated food jar so it’s still warm at lunch.
equipment: insulated food jar for each child
kettle or pot for boiling water
steps: Cook the ravioli the night before as the package directs, drain, toss with the sauce, and refrigerate it within 2 hours. (Or cook it fresh in the morning.)
In the morning, fill each insulated food jar with boiling water, put the lid on, and let it stand a few minutes (USDA).
Meanwhile, reheat the ravioli and sauce on the stove until it is steaming hot and reads 165°F on a food thermometer.
Pour the water out of the jar, fill it with the hot ravioli, sprinkle with Parmesan and close the lid tightly. Keep it closed until lunch so the food stays at 140°F or above (USDA).
recipes.make_ahead: Cook the ravioli the night before; reheat it in the morning.

freezer.text: Reheat cooked pasta from the refrigerator, not frozen, for a thermos lunch.

leftovers.text: Whatever comes home uneaten from a lunch box gets thrown away, along with used bags and wrappers (USDA).

recipes.kids: Kids can help sprinkle the cheese and close the jar. A grown-up handles the boiling water.

swaps.soup: The same thermos steps work for soup, chili or mac and cheese.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the ravioli the night before.
